statement: A scoring rule must be decidable from what the attestation binds, and a tree-only proxy for unbound state must be measured before it ships. In cejel #535 a workflow confined to master in a repository whose default branch is main earned B3 PR-gate credit. The default branch is ref state; the only repository revision Cejel's attestation binds is the commit (repo.headSha), and ref state is not a function of it; an earlier sentence read from refs made cejel issue refuse honest reproductions (#540). The obvious tree-only proxy, uncredit a workflow whose branch filters name master and not main, fired on 3 of 23 public corpus rows (fastapi, express, guava), all of whose default branch is master: every removal would have been a false assertion of absence. Rules: check the attestation binds a property before scoring from it; measure any proxy on real repositories; ship nothing that removes true credit; hand the options to the operator.

When two criteria make the same kind of claim about one input, decide it with one shared predicate plus a test that they agree. In cejel, v27 (#517) stopped B3 crediting a publish-only CI workflow, but B2 kept counting every CI file as PR-trace credit (#527). The fix routes both through one function built from the existing allowlist readers, and a test asserts, for every fixture where neither criterion abstains (abstaining fixtures are skipped), that B2's note names the workflows B3's note names and that B2's credited count equals the CI files minus B3's uncredited count. Review then found the shared reader itself assumed bash: on a Windows runner pwsh runs `echo @{x=./t.ps1}` (#564), so a shared predicate shares its defects too. Sharing also cut repeated reads: in one run on one machine, a v27 scan of eight 480 KB workflows fell from 1.46 s to 1.19 s.
